samples.question: This picture shows three grey pipes on a white page and three solid grey panels lying on top of them. A panel is opaque, so wherever a pipe runs behind a panel it is hidden. Each pipe runs from a small black dot on the left edge to a coloured square on the right edge; one pipe ends at the blue square, one at the orange square and one at the purple square. A pipe never bends behind a panel: behind a panel it is one straight run that carries on in exactly the direction it had when it went in, and it comes out heading the same way. Pipes cross each other only behind a panel; wherever you can see them they never touch. One black dot is circled by a black ring. How high a pipe starts, how high a square sits and how near the ring a square looks do not matter; only which pipe joins to which square counts. Follow the pipe that starts at the ringed dot. Which coloured square is at its far end? Answer blue, orange, or purple.
